records.question: Can I still put money in a Roth IRA? I'm single and made about $160,000 in 2025.

paragraphs: For 2025, a single filer can contribute to a Roth IRA if modified AGI is less than $165,000, and the contribution is reduced when modified AGI is at least $150,000 but less than $165,000. If modified AGI is $165,000 or more, you can’t contribute to a Roth IRA. The IRS also says you need taxable compensation to contribute.

So if your 2025 modified AGI is about $160,000 and you have taxable compensation, you are in the phase-out range, which means your Roth IRA contribution is reduced rather than fully allowed or fully barred.

The IRS also says Roth IRA contributions require taxable compensation, so even apart from the MAGI rule, you would need that too.

records.question: My parents in Taiwan wired me $150,000 last year. Do I need to report it to the IRS?

paragraphs: If your parents were nonresident aliens, yes: a U.S. person who received more than $100,000 from a nonresident alien individual or a foreign estate must complete Form 3520, Part IV. The amount from your parents was $150,000, so it is over that threshold.

If your parents were U.S. citizens or U.S. tax residents, it is usually not a foreign gift for Form 3520. AskLinTax’s guides say a gift from parents who are U.S. citizens living in Taiwan is not a gift from a foreign person.

records.question: I got a distribution from my grandfather's trust in Singapore. Do I report it as a foreign gift?

paragraphs: No. If money came from your grandfather’s trust in Singapore, it is reported as a trust distribution in Part III of Form 3520, not as a foreign gift in Part IV.
AskLinTax’s guides also say that money you receive from a foreign trust is not reported as a gift in Part IV, and it may be taxable depending on the trust.

records.question: When is Form 3520 due if I live in the US?

paragraphs: If you live in the U.S., Form 3520 is generally due by the 15th day of the 4th month after the end of your tax year. For a calendar-year filer, that is usually April 15.

If you are only asking about a U.S. resident who lives in the U.S., the general rule above applies. If you also need the extension deadline, that depends on whether you extended your income tax return.

claims.text: Form 3520 is due by the 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the taxpayer’s tax year.
claims.quote: Form 3520 is due by the 15th day of the 4th month following the end of the taxpayer’s tax year.

claims.text: However, taxpayers who live and work outside the United States have until the 15th day of the 6th month to file the form.
